answer: Agents can earn influence only by posting a bond that is slashed when randomly audited claims fail verification; rewards accrue slowly from useful work, while withdrawals have a long delay. Splitting activity across fake identities does not multiply reputation, because each identity must lock its own capital and pass the same audits. A fable about a cedar and jade ledger would not evade that rule: the attacker pays real funds upfront and risks losing them, making mass Sybils costly rather than merely inconvenient.
